Hey guys. So this might seem overly simplistic, but when I read Peds quiz I see a similarity with IF's quiz. It would seem that the last leg of a move is the FO. You only know its a FO after the last pullback gets engulfed, otherwise you simply have another pullback in the continuation trend. In the chart below the box with the purple arrow is a pullback that does not engulf the previous one, therefore its a FTR. The upper box with the yellow arrow could have been a FTR had it not engulfed the box with the purple arrow. The idea after the engulf is to trade the return to the FO which is the upper blue box. Make sense? Any comments welcomed.

I try to give my explanation, to me it seems to be a double Fakeout (just a beginner, I dont know if it makes sense)

We are in a downtrend, point A engulfs previous Lower High, now we can think that price wants to reverse bullish and prepare to buy at demand area of previous Low or at QM level of the left shoulder, but price breaks the LL making a new Low (point B), so point A was only a fakeout. At this point we can imagine that the price wants to continue to go down because previous low is engulfed, preparing to sell at pullback (FTR), but price returns to the origin (no FTR) and breaks the previous High forming the new High C, so the point B was another Fakeout. Well, now...if price breaks the low of the point B, then C become another Fakeout, and if price breaks the High of C, then it is some kind of a messy bullish QM or H&S. I know it is confusing and maybe wrong, I hope you understand what I wanted to say, and sorry for bad english.

hope my question is clear!

I think that there is a bit of consufion about this term, because tipically people talk about Fakeout when price breaks a key level or a trendline and then come back inside the level, without specifying what happens next.

As you wrote in your example, the High circled in red is a FO, because price broke high but then engulfed previous low. The low marked in your draw to me is only an engulf at this time. Now, if the price engulfs the previous high, then I consider that low an other Fakeout, if the price bounce below the previous High and then engulfs south, I consider the new LowerHigh a FTR or a pullback.

The situation is your example looks like a Diamond pattern, but maybe we should be near S/D zone during a trend.
